SECTION - I                  PREAMBLE, SHORT TITLE,  COMMENCEMENT AND APPLICATION

ABOUT UNIVERSITY    Vidyashilp University is the culmination of an outstanding legacy of the Vidyashilp  Education Group, committed to excellence in education. Vidyashilp University aims to  foster an environment and culture of collaboration, responsiveness, high performance and  service. We are people-centred and have a strongly desire to provide a unique Vidyashilp  Experience to our students and staff, focused on nurturing students who will become self- aware, confident, empathetic and resourceful leaders who will serve society to the best of  their abilities.    The VU Experience fosters a climate for collaboration between individuals and groups from  diverse cultures and backgrounds. VU creates a diverse, inclusive community and  environment where VU faculty, staff, students and parents, and alumni feel connected to  one another by a common sense of purpose, pride, and spirit, and develop a distinctive  ability to work, learn, lead and serve in diverse contexts.    VU’s primary ed

ucational goal is the cultivation of deep domain knowledge within each  student’s chosen field. We believe that investing in all domains of our differentiated focus  areas is essential to create intellectual capital to drive progress and achieve excellence. At  VU, our schools don’t function in silos but rather with an interdisciplinary dependence.  We focus on a problem -solving approach and provide program choices across all four  schools with a curriculum established in Data Science, Digital Business, Design Studies,  Legal Studies and Liberal Arts.    VISION, MISSION AND CORE VALUES  OUR VISION  We aspire to provide meaningful, collective learning experiences that result in  conscientious leadership for a progressive, yet sustainable society.  OUR MISSION  x We inspire people locally, nationally and globally by extending access to Vidyashilp  University’s innovative teaching and resources through inclusive and flexible  opportunities to study and research.  x To develop human val
ues and human potential to its fullest extent so that  intellectually capable and imaginatively gifted leaders can emerge in a range of  professions.  1

OUR VALUES  INTEGRITY – We embrace integrity as a central value in all aspects of personal and  professional engagement – including learning, teaching, governance and service – to instil  a culture of trust and accountability.      ACADEMIC FREEDOM – We affirm the principles of academic freedom for both students  and teachers, their rights and responsibilities to advance knowledge through research and  creativity, and to educate students to develop their own independence of mind.    DIVERSITY, EQUITY AND INCLUSION  – We assert that diversity and interplay of  differences is essential to educational excellence and to enrich the individual and collective  learning experiences.  Short Title, Commencement and Application    a. These Regulations shall be called Academic Regulations.  b. They shall come into force with immediate effect.   c. The Academic Regulations are applicable to all existing Degree and Diploma  Programs of the University. Any amendments made therein, shall also be ap

plicable  to new Degree and Diploma Programs that may be offered by the University in the  future.    d. Specific aspects of the Regulations pertaining to a particular Degree Program are  given separately along with the concerned Program Regulations.     e. These Regulations may evolve and get amended or modified or changed through  appropriate approvals from the Academic Council, from time to time, and shall be  binding on all concerned.    f. Additional Regulations, if any, prescribed by the Regulatory / Statutory Bodies for  a particular Degree Program shall be included in the concerned Program  Regulations.      Definitions    In these Regulations, unless the context otherwise requires:   a) “Academic Calendar” means the schedule of academic and miscellaneous events as  approved by the Academic Council;  b) “Academic Council” means the Academic Council of the University;  c) “Academic Regulations” means the Academic Regulations of the University;  d) “Academic Term” means a
Semester or Summer Term;  e) “Act” means the Vidyashilp University Act, 2020;  f) “Board of Governors” means the Board of Governors of University as specified by  the Act;  2

g) “Board of Management” means the Board of Management of University as  specified by the Act;  h) “BoS” means the Board of Studies of a particular School / Department / Program  of the University;  i) “Clause” means duly numbered Clauses of these Regulations;  j) “Course” means, a specific subject usually identified by its Course  number and  Course title, with specified credits and a Course Plan, taught by some  teacher(s)/Course-instructor(s) to a specific class (group of students) during a  specific academic term/semester;  k) “Course Instructor” means, the teacher/faculty member or the Course instructor  of a Course;  l) “Dean” means the Dean of School / Centre of the University;  m)“Degree Program” includes all Degree Programs;  n) “Program Chair” means the Program Chair / Head of the Department / School  within the University;  o) “PAC” means, the Program Academic Committee of a concerned Program of Study  of the University;   p) “Program Regulations” means the Program

Regulations governing a specific Degree  Program offered by the University, and includes the set of Program -Specific  Regulations, Program Structure and Curriculum;  q) “Program Structure and Curriculum” means the components of the Program  Curriculum, Courses with Credits and the mandatory minimum credits to be  earned in each component for the award of the degree;  r) “Registrar” means the Registrar of the University;  s) “Registrar (Evaluation)” means the Registrar (Evaluation) of the University;  t) “School/Department” means a constituent School / Department / Centre of the  University established for monitoring, supervising and guiding, teaching, training  and research activities in broadly related fields of studies;    u) “Section” means duly numbered Sections of these Regulations;    v) “Statutes” means the Statues of Vidyashilp University;    w) “Sub-Clause” means duly numbered Sub-Clauses of these Regulations;    x) "Summer Term” means an additional academic term con

ducted during the summer  break (typically in June-July) for a duration of about eight (08) calendar weeks;    y) “University / VU” means Vidyashilp University; and  z) “Vice Chancellor” means the Vice Chancellor of the University.      3

         1 ADMISSION Admission to the Universityshall be open to all persons irrespective of caste, class, creed, gender, abilities, or nationality. All admissions shall be made on the basis of merit in the qualifying examinations and as per the rules and guidelines prescribed by the Government of Karnataka, other concerned regulatory bodies and the entrance examinations conducted by the University. The students shall be admitted to a Program subject to fulfilment of eligibility criteria, as prescribed by the University for the respective Program. A student admitted to a Program of study, shall continue to remain registered for such a Program, till they successfully complete the Program or withdraw from the Program in accordance with the concerned Program Regulations. Every student duly admitted to the University for a Program after compliance with prescribed formalities and payment of prescribed fees as applicable and other amounts and submission of prescribed documents and certifi

cates shall be allotted a University Enrolment Number OR UEN. If a student fails to pay the University Fee, or fails to produce all the mandatory documents and certificates required for admission to the University before the prescribed last date, the Provisional Offer of Admission to the student shall stand withdrawn. If a student desires to join the University on the basis of Lateral Entry or Transfer of Credits from other Institutes/Universities during the Program, they shall be examined for eligibility for admission as per the procedure and criteria laid down in the Academic Regulations of the University and the concerned Program Regulations, and admission shall be dependent on their eligibility so determined. Confirmation of admission and enrolment in the University is subject to fulfilment of the eligibility criteria. 2 FEE POLICY a. The University fee consists of components such as Tuition Fee, Security Deposit (Refundable), Examination Fee, Convocation Fee and such other compone

nts as may be prescribed by the Board of Management from time to time. b. Every program of the University has a prescribed University Fee. Further the Fee Structure and the payment schedule for the entire duration of the concerned program is announced by way of notification before the commencement of each academic year. c. The Tuition Fee always means the Annual Tuition Fee for an academic year for a program. The Annual Tuition Fee does not include the expenses / charges for extra- curricular activities, local / international educational trips and other value-added programs that may be introduced from time to time. 7

d. The Security Deposit is a Refundable Security Deposit without any interest, subject  to deduction of outstanding dues if any, after the student graduates from the program  or discontinues from the program or for whatever the reason(s).  e. The Payment Schedule of the University Fee must be strictly adhered to, by all the  students. Failure to comply shall result in the student not being eligible for  registration to the concerned academic year and late fee will be charged accordingly.  Further, the students are cautioned that this could lead to the loss of an academic  year.  f. Vidyashilp University shall not be obliged to send any reminders for payment of the  University Fee. If it is done, it is only in the interest of students and cannot be  demanded or referred to in the event of failure to pay the University Fee as per the  specified schedule.  g. The University Fee Structure is subject to change from time to time and shall be  notified by the University. The University’s

decision regarding changes in fee structure  is final and binding on all concerned.    3 PAYMENT OF UNIVERSITY FEE    a. For Students who seek admission directly in the University:    Students who seek admission directly for a specific program in the University shall be  notified of the prescribed University Fee and schedule of payment for first year and  subsequent years in the Provisional Admission Letter. Failure to remit the fee as per  the specified payment schedule or commencement of each academic year, shall result  in the forfeiture of admission to the program and applicability of late fee accordingly  as decided by the University time to time.    b. For General Students admitted through CET of Government of Karnataka:  [i] The Fee Structure (Engineering Fee Structure for CET Fee) for students  admitted through CET shall be as notified by the Karnataka Examinations  Authority (KEA).  First year’s tuition fee shall be remitted to the CET -KEA at  the time of counselling / sea

t selection.   [ii]  On reporting to the University for confirmation of admission to the concerned  program, the student shall also remit “other fees” as notified by the University  from time to time.   [iii]   Subsequent years’ tuition and other fee s shall be remitted directly to the  University on or before the notified last date. Failure to remit “other fee s”  notified by the university, shall result in the forfeiture of admission to the  program and charge of the late fee as may be prescribed.  c. For category (SC/ST/others as specified by KEA) students admitted through CET of  Government of Karnataka:  8

[i]        The Fee Structure (Engineering Fee Structure for CET Fee) for students admitted  through CET shall be as notified by the Karnataka Examinations Authority  (KEA).    [ii]     On reporting to the University for confirmation of admission to the concerned  program, the student shall remit “other fees” as notified by the University.  [iii]   Further, such student(s) shall compulsorily require to apply for/renew the  Scholarship as notified by the Government of Karnataka.  Upon receipt of  scholarship from the Government of Karnataka, such Student(s) shall promptly  remit the scholarship amount towards the fee to the University within five (05)  working days on receipt of the scholarship from the Government of Karnataka.    It is the sole responsibility of the student(s) to comply with the norms for payment of Fee  within the stipulated time. Failure to pay the University Fee / scholarship amount as per  the specified schedule shall result in (i) the student being declared inel ig

ible for  registration to the term end exams, which could result in loss of an academic year; (ii) levy  late fee for late remittance(s); (iii) in case of SC/ST/OBC students, a Report will be sent to  the Government of Karnataka about non -remittance of scholarship amount to the  University towards the fee and misuse of the same.    4     PAYMENT PROCEDURE    a. All fee payments should necessarily be made online only using the login credentials  of the fee portal as instructed by the University from time to time.  b. The Fee is payable in INR only  c. The University will not accept Cash, DD and Cheque.  d. The digital receipt will be generated by the online system subject to realization of  payments.  e. All statutory taxes / government levies, convenience charges and bank charges  pertaining to inward remittance of any fee, if any, shall be borne by the payer.  f. The University shall not be responsible for any fee amount returned to the payer  (Student) without being credited t

o Vidyashilp University bank account. In such  cases, late fee as may be prescribed shall be applicable till the date of receipt of the  fee by Vidyashilp University.  g. It shall be the sole responsibility of the student to ensure that the fee payment  process is completed within the specified time.  In case a student is required to repeat/re -register for an Academic Year, the Annual Fee  payable by her/him shall correspond to the Academic Year to be repeated, and shall be  as per the Fee Policy in force at that point of time.  The policies relating to the University Fee and Deposits, where applicable, are the  prerogative of Vidyashilp University and may be revised by the University from time to  time. Such changes shall be binding on all concerned.  9

5   FEE CONCESSION AND SCHOLARSHIP POLICY  Introduction:  Vidyashilp University is committed for providing the best education opportunities to  motivated students. The University has established various categories of scholarships to  encourage and enable students to pursue education at Vidyashilp University.   Scholarships are provided to reward and support meritorious and talented students, who  have demonstrated exceptional performance in academics, sports and co-curricular  activities. The University is particularly committed to enabling meritorious students with  financial constraints, differently abled students and achievers at the state and national  levels, through appropriate scholarships.   5.1 Categories of Scholarships    To cater to the different needs and circumstances of meritorious students, the University  offers four (04) categories of Scholarships.      5.1.1 Merit-based Scholarship at the time of Admission    Merit scholarships are awarded to students with outstand

ing academic  performance. This scholarship is awarded at the time of admission to the 1 st year  of a program.     Two (02) sub-categories of Merit Scholarships are offered:     5.1.2 Outstanding achievement in State / National / International Level Entrance  Examinations:    This Scholarship is awarded based on the performance in the State / National /  International Level Entrance Examinations specified for a particular program.     5.1.3 Meritorious Performance in the Qualifying Examination:    The Scholarship is awarded based on the performance in the Qualifying  Examinations (State / National / International Boards).  The details of the extent  of scholarship and the corresponding eligibility criteria are as per the scholarship  policy and subject to approval by the Scholarship Committee.    5.2 Enabling Scholarship    The University is committed to ensure that a meritorious student is not hindered  from pursuing education at Vidyashilp due to financial constraints.     Three (
03) sub-categories of enabling scholarships are offered:        10

5.2.1 Low Income Based Scholarship     This scholarship is offered to enable meritorious students whose family income is  a constraint to meet the tuition fees of the program.    5.2.2 Single Parent (Mother) Income Based Scholarship.     This Scholarship is specifically offered to a student with Single  Parent (Mother)   having financial constraints to pursue education at Vidyashilp.    5.2.3 Ex-Service Parent Income Based Scholarship    This scholarship is offered to a meritorious student whose parent (father/mother)  is an ex-service personnel with financial constraints.     The definition of ex-service is specific to commissioned/non-commissioned staff of  the Armed Forces and staff of the Central/State Police Services.    5.2.4 The details of the extent of scholarship and the corresponding eligibility criteria are  as per the scholarship policy and subject to approval by the Scholarship  Committee.    5.3  Encouragement Scholarship    This scholarship is awarded to recognize an

d encourage students who have excelled in  various sports / culture / fine arts/ s ciences and have participated / been awarded at  State/ National / International levels.     The University is also committed to encourage differently -abled students to pursue  education at Vidyashilp University.     Two (02) sub-categories of Encouragement Scholarships are offered:    5.3.1 Scholarship for Outstanding performance in the fields of Sports/Culture/Fine  Arts/Sciences.    5.3.2 Scholarship for Differently-Abled.    5.3.3 The details of the extent of scholarship and the corresponding eligibility criteria are  as per the scholarship policy  and subject to approval by the Scholarship  Committee.      5.4 Academic Performance Scholarship (During the Program)  To reward and motivate excellence in overall academic performance, scholarships are  awarded to the selected outstanding students during the program i.e., from 2nd Year  onwards. The details of the extent of scholarship and the corresp
onding eligibility criteria  are as per the scholarship policy and subject to approval by the Scholarship Committee.    11

5.5 General Terms and Conditions    a) All types of Scholarships shall be applicable only on the Tuition Fee for the  concerned academic year.  b) A student shall be eligible for only one scholarship in a given academic year.  c) All types of Scholarships shall be valid only for the concerned academic year.   d) Renewal of any type of scholarship is not automatic and shall be governed by the  terms and criteria as mentioned in this policy.  e) The number of Scholarships to be awarded under each type and sub -category for  the concerned academic year shall be solely decided by the Board of Management  on the recommendation of the University Scholarship Committee.  f) A student who has been selected for a scholarship shall provide a joint (with  parent) undertaking.     The scholarship shall be terminated and the scholarship amount shall be returned to the  University, in case of the following violations;    i) Any information provided in the scholarship application form is found

to be  untrue or fraudulent;   ii) Found guilty and penalized under any disciplinary action;  iii)Withdraws/discontinues studies at the University (The withdrawal process shall  not be completed unless the scholarship amount is fully returned).    Further, such a student shall not be eligible to re-apply for any University scholarship.    5.6 Scholarship Process    a) During Admissions:  i) Eligible candidates may submit the scholarship application form with all  relevant documents to the admission office.    ii) The University Scholarship Committee shall scrutinize and shortlist candidates  to be interviewed by the Committee.  iii)The award of scholarship shall be recommended by the University Scholarship  Committee for the approval of the Vice Chancellor.  iv) The decision of the Vice Chancellor shall be final.  b) During the Program:  i) The University Scholarship Committee shall invite applications at the  commencement of an academic year for the Academic Performance  Sc

holarships which are awarded based on performance during the previous  academic year.   ii) The committee shall also invite applications for renewal of Enabling,  Encouraging Scholarships which was provided at the time of admissions and  the same shall be subject to review by the Scholarship Committee.  The committee shall recommend the list of scholarship awardees to the Vice Chancellor  for approval and the decision of the Vice-Chancellor shall be final.  12
SECTION  - III                      ACADEMIC REGULATIONS     Amended Academic Regulations approved in the 6th Meeting of the Academic Council held  on July 29, 2025 vide Resolution No 6.16.  13

Academic Calendar     1.1. The academic activities of the University are regulated by the Academic  Calendar approved by the Academic Council and notified by the  University at least one calendar month before the commencement of each  academic year.     1.2. An academic year in the University shall normally be divided into two  semesters consisting of ninety (90) University working days each, known  as ‘Odd Semester’ (normally from July / August to December) and ‘Even  Semester’ (normally from January to April/May).  1.3. An additional Academic Term known as the ‘Summer Term’ may be  scheduled during the summer break (June to July).  2. Registration    2.1. Every student shall complete the mandatory requirement known as the  ‘Registration’ procedure and register for the prescribed and approved  Courses to be pursued during a given Academic Term. This Registration  process is mandatory every Semester / Academic Term till the  completion of the Program. The University Registrar's Of

fice manages the  registration process and related activities.    2.2. The prescribed date for Registration shall be announced in the Academic  Calendar and through notifications issued by the University to this  effect.    2.3. The Chairperson of the Program Academic Committee (PAC) of each  Program/School shall communicate the list of approved/prescribed  Courses available for Registration in the concerned Semester to the   University Registrar's Office for Notification as per the specified dates in  the Academic Calendar.     2.4. Every student after consulting their Faculty Advisor [Mentor] is required  to register for the approved Courses offered in the given Academic Term  at the commencement of each Semester/Academic Term on the days  fixed for such registration as notified in the Academic Calendar or the  University Notification to this effect.    On joining the University, each student is assigned a Faculty Advisor  [Mentor] to counsel the student on matters related to the

Registration  process.     2.5.   Without registration, any academic activity (Course / Internship / Project, etc.) undergone by a student will not be counted towards the requirements for the award of the Degree. No student shall be permitted to attend classes without completing the appropriate registration procedure. 15

2.6. Late registration shall only be permitted in case of  medical exigencies,  specifically hospitalization, trauma or contagious disease s, for the  student / family member , and participation in approved  competitions/events as detailed in Sub-Clauses 2.6.1 and 2.6.2. below.  In such cases, a student may be permitted for late registration with prior  approval from the concerned Program Chair / Dean of the concerned  School.  In the absence of Program Chair / Dean of the concerned School,  the authorised faculty shall approve.     2.6.1.In cases of medical exigency (viz. hospitalization, trauma or  contagious disease only),  for the student / family member,  the  maximum period permissible for late registration shall not be more  than two (02) calendar weeks counted from the specified date of  Registration announced by the University.  The student must  produce the medical certificates, medical prescriptions, hospital  discharge report, medical fitness report and all such rele vant

documents duly attested by the concerned registered medical  officer of the hospital where the concerned student / family  member was hospitalized or medically treated. The student shall  not be eligible for late registration if they fail to produce authentic  medical certificates and relevant documents in support of the  medical exigency.  2.6.2.If a student of second and subsequent semesters has been selected  / permitted by the University to participate in State / National /  International Competitions / Events, the concerned student may  be permitted for late registration.  The student must produce duly  attested documents and/or Certificates to be eligible for the  provision of late registration. The number of days for which the  concerned student shall be given permission for late registration  shall be approved by the Vice Chancellor on recommendation of  both the Director, Campus Life and Program Chair of the  concerned school.  2.7. In case of any other reason for late reg

istration other than the cases  specified in Sub -Clauses 2.6.1 and 2.6.2 above, the maximum  permissible period for late registration shall not be more than one (01)  calendar week counted from the specified date of Registration announced  by the University.     Further, the student shall pay a Late Fee for late registration as specified  by the University at the commencement of the Academic Term. No  16

relaxation whatsoever shall be given on attendance requirement in case  of late registration. Under no circumstances shall such a student be  permitted to register for the Academic Term after the permissible period  for late registration of one (01) calendar week counted from the specified  date of Registration.    2.8. Further, the provisions mentioned in Clauses 2.6 and 2.7 are applicable  only for registration at the commencement of a Semester and does not  apply for the Summer Term (Refer Section 11).  2.9. Students are not permitted to re -register for Courses which they have  already passed, except under the provisions and conditions of Clauses  11.4.3 and 12.5.    2.10. A student shall be permitted to register in the next Semester only if all  the following conditions are fulfilled:     2.10.1.The student has paid all specified fees of the University as per the  University Fee Policy and payment schedule.  2.10.2.The student has cleared all University, Hostel, Transport and

Library dues (if any).  2.10.3.The student has not been debarred from registering on any  specific grounds by the University.   2.11. Further, the student must fulfil the progression criteria prescribed in  Clause 12.1 to register for the Semester at the commencement of the  concerned Academic Year.    2.12. A student who is eligible for registration, but fails to register for the  Academic Term within the specified dates, including the late registration  date, shall be removed from the rolls for the concerned Academic Term  and shall not be permitted to attend classes for the concerned Academic  Term. Such a student shall have to register for the corresponding  Academic Term in the next academic year.    2.13. Pre-Registration (Specialization / Minor / Open and other specified  Courses) for higher Semesters:     All students (other than the students admitted to the first Semester of a  Program) intending to register for the next higher Semester are required  to complete the Pre
-Registration process. A student, after consultation  with the Faculty Advisor [Mentor], is required to declare their intent to  17

register for Specialization / Minor / Open and any other specified  Courses, as/if applicable, well in advance, before the actual start of the  concerned Academic Term, through the process of Pre -Registration as  per the schedule/dates announced in the Academic Calendar and/or the  notifications issued by the University to this effect. Specialization /  Minor courses will be offered only if a minimum of ten (10) students  register for the same. However, the program chair may permit to offer the  courses at their discretion.     2.14. Course Pre-Requisites    For a student to register for some Courses, it may be required either to  have exposure in, or to have completed satisfactorily, or to have prior  earned credits in some specified Courses. Such Course pre -requisites  shall be specified in the concerned Program  Regulations / Course Plan  as approved by the PAC.    2.15. Changes in Registration: Add/Drop     Students may add and drop Courses after consulting the concerned  Facul

ty Advisors [Mentor]  and submit a request for add/drop to the  concerned Program Chair/Dean of Schools within two weeks of  commencement of classes for add/drop.      On approval, the Course(s) shall be added, and the dropped Course(s)  will not appear on the Grade Card (Refer Clause 8.14).      Student may seek transfer from one Program to another before the  commencement of registration for the Second Year with due approval of  both Program Chairs, subject to the eligibility criteria and provisions of  the academic regulations.  On no account shall a transfer from one  Program to another be allowed beyond the stipulated period.    2.16. A student of a particular degree Program shall register for the  appropriate number of Course credits in each Semester/session that is  within the minimum and maximum limits specific to that degree Program  as stipulated in the Program Regulations.    2.17. Audit a Course    Auditing a Course is a provision for a student who may opt to register for

a Course to acquire knowledge / skills, but not to earn credits and grade  points.    A student who desires to register for auditing a Course shall consult their  Faculty Advisor [Mentor]  and seek approval of the concerned Course  18

Instructor (Refer Clause 8.1). Registration shall only be permitted as per  the criteria and guidelines prescribed by the concerned Course  Instructor and duly approved by the concerned PAC.
